note_on_batch_selection: This batch was routed as a FIGURE-fidelity batch, but PDF pages 177-199 (printed pages 147-169, clause 8.4.6 through 8.6.4) contain NO general formats, syntax skeletons, or diagrams of any kind - they are continuous prose plus numbered/dashed lists. scripts/spec/page_workunit.py itself reported '0 with figure content' for all 12 slices. The likely cause is a printed-page vs PDF-page-index confusion: the printed page numbers 177-199 correspond to PDF pages 207-229, which is where the figure-bearing material in this region actually lives. No choice-indicator (vertical bar), unclosed brace/bracket, ellipsis-placement, or underlining check was applicable on any page in this batch.

findings.pdf_says: The whole block from 'NOTE   The UTF-16 format of ISO/IEC 10646 is a coded character set ...' through '... consistent with the needs of their application.' is printed in the smaller NOTE typeface and indented to the body margin of numbered item 2). This includes the two dashed sub-items and BOTH trailing paragraphs: 'These techniques facilitate efficient processing of data as fixed-size two-octet code elements, but present opportunities for corruption of data if not handled correctly. To achieve a better understanding, see ISO/IEC 10646.' and 'COBOL does not provide any special handling or recognition of surrogate pairs; nor does COBOL provide recognition of composite sequences. Each two-octet code element of UTF-16 is treated in COBOL as though it were itself a character. Users are responsible for ensuring that any truncation, replacement, or reference-modification that occurs is consistent with the needs of their application.' Font-size measurement at 300 dpi confirms both trailing paragraphs are set in the same reduced NOTE face as the 'NOTE' paragraph and are markedly smaller than item 2)'s own text.
findings.markdown_says: Only the first paragraph carries the NOTE label ('NOTE The UTF-16 format of ISO/IEC 10646 is a coded character set ...'). The two dashed sub-items and then both trailing paragraphs are emitted flush at top level, unindented and unlabelled, so 'These techniques facilitate efficient processing of data ...' and 'COBOL does not provide any special handling or recognition of surrogate pairs; ...' read as ordinary normative body prose of 8.5.1.4, at the same level as the clause's own requirements.
findings.why_it_matters: In ISO documents a NOTE is informative, not normative. Flattening the NOTE's continuation paragraphs into body prose silently promotes them to apparent requirements. The promoted text is directly load-bearing for this compiler's UTF-16/alphanumeric-repertoire decisions ('COBOL does not provide any special handling or recognition of surrogate pairs ... Each two-octet code element of UTF-16 is treated in COBOL as though it were itself a character'), so a reader deriving behaviour from the markdown could cite it as a shall-level rule and could also mis-scope it: in the PDF the entire NOTE hangs off numbered item 2) of 8.5.1.4, not off the clause as a whole.
findings.suggested_repair: Re-attach the whole NOTE block to item 2) of 8.5.1.4 and keep it visibly informative: indent the dashed sub-items and both trailing paragraphs under the NOTE paragraph (or repeat a 'NOTE (continued)'/blockquote marker) so the non-normative boundary ends where the PDF's reduced typeface ends.

findings.pdf_says: '8.5.1.4   Limitations of character handling' and '8.5.1.5   Algebraic signs' are printed as fourth-level clause headings, subordinate to '8.5.1  Computer independent data description', in the same typographic rank as their siblings 8.5.1.1 General, 8.5.1.2 Files and records and 8.5.1.3 Levels.
findings.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 7977 '## 8.5.1.4 Limitations of character handling' and line 7996 '## 8.5.1.5 Algebraic signs' - level 2 - while their parent is line 7901 '### 8.5.1 Computer independent data description' (level 3) and their siblings are line 7904 '#### 8.5.1.1 General', 7911 '#### 8.5.1.2 Files and records', 7922 '#### 8.5.1.3 Levels' (level 4). The children are therefore one level SHALLOWER than the clause that contains them, i.e. the outline is inverted, and they sit at the same level as the '## Page N' scaffolding heading.
findings.why_it_matters: Any table of contents, outline view, or anchor-based navigation generated from the markdown misrepresents the standard's clause hierarchy - subclauses detach from their parent clause and appear as peers of clause 8.5 or of the page furniture. For a spec used as the citation authority, a reader following the outline can attribute a rule to the wrong clause. The same inversion recurs across this batch and beyond, so it is a mechanical transcription defect, not a local slip.

verification_notes: Every prose paragraph, numbered item and dashed item on all 12 pages was compared word-for-word against the 300 dpi render; no missing, added or altered normative text was found.

All cross-references were crop-zoomed to native resolution and confirmed: p181 '8.1.2, Computer's coded character set' and '9.1, Files'; p187 '8.4.2.3, Subscripts'; p189 '8.3.3.6, Figurative constant values, General rule 3' and '14.9.39, SET statement' with 'EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL'; p191 '8.5.1.12.2, Positional correspondence'; p197 'Clause 10, Structured compilation group' and '8.4.6, Scope of names'; p199 '14.6.2.3.2, Initial state', '14.6.2.4, Initial state of object data', '9.3.1, Objects and classes, 9.3.9, Class inheritance, and 9.3.14, Object life cycle', '8.5.1.9, Dynamic-capacity tables'.

The PDF's own wording was preserved where it is itself imperfect - e.g. p197 item 5) 'in which the number of characters positions is zero' is transcribed verbatim; this is an ISO typo, not a transcription defect, and must not be 'corrected'.

Pages 189 and 199 end mid-sentence in the PDF and the markdown slice carries the sentence to completion (the remainder belongs to the following page). That is page-boundary joining, not lost or duplicated text.

Running-header representation varies across the batch ('# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' on 181/183/185/187/197, '**ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)**' on 177/179/191/199, unmarked on 193, absent on 195). Treated as page-break furniture per the run's exclusion list and not reported as a finding.
